title: Fajr, the dawn prayer
hook: the dawn prayer, the hardest and the most rewarded
tomorrow: what does Dadi say on the porch before the sun is even up?

segments.voice: Yesterday, five posts driven into the ground, fifty become five. The day has a frame. Today, the first post, and the hardest one to reach.
screen: `THE DAY HAS A FRAME.` → `THE FIRST POST.`

segments.voice: An alarm named "actually get up" still loses to a warm blanket most mornings. Now here's the odd thing in the call to prayer, the adhan. Five times a day it goes out with the same lines: God is greatest, come to prayer, come to success. Except at dawn. At Fajr, in the Sunni call, the caller adds a line heard at no other time of day: as-salatu khayrun min an-nawm. Prayer is better than sleep. Why say it only once a day?
screen: `THE ALARM LOSES.` → `FIVE CALLS, THE SAME LINES.` → `ONE EXTRA LINE AT DAWN.`

segments.voice: Look at who's listening. At midday, at sunset, at night, the people hearing the call are awake. At dawn, the listener is in bed. So the extra line isn't for the street; it's for the pillow. It answers the argument going on under the blanket, out loud, before you've had time to lose it. In a report kept by Abu Dawud, the Prophet ﷺ teaches the call to a young caller named Abu Mahdhura, and tells him to add this line at the dawn prayer. Shia Muslims don't use the line in their call; they hold that it wasn't part of the original adhan. Both pray Fajr, and both know the fight with sleep. And the hadith don't pretend it's easy. In Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet says Fajr and 'Isha are the heaviest prayers for the hypocrites, and that if people knew what was in them, they'd come even crawling. In Sahih Muslim he says the two short rak'ahs before Fajr are better than the world and everything in it. Hardest, and most rewarded, in the same breath. Then one more line, for the mornings sleep wins: whoever sleeps through a prayer should pray it when they wake. Not wait for tomorrow. Get up, and pray it then.
screen: `THE LINE IS FOR THE PILLOW.` · `TAUGHT TO ABU MAHDHURA.` · `HEAVIEST, AND BETTER THAN THE WORLD.` · `SLEPT THROUGH? PRAY ON WAKING.` · then, large: `PRAYER IS BETTER THAN SLEEP.`

segments.voice: Sit up the way you would at dawn: feet flat on the floor, back off the pillow. Say the line out loud, slowly, in Arabic or in English: prayer is better than sleep. Then sit and listen to whatever part of you argues back, without answering it.
screen: `FEET ON THE FLOOR.` · `SAY THE LINE ALOUD.` · `LET THE ARGUMENT TALK.`

segments.voice: Fajr: dawn, and the prayer said at first light, before sunrise. The only call of the day that talks to someone still asleep.
For tomorrow's alarm: prayer is better than sleep, said to the pillow at first light. First post, set.

screen: `DAY 1668 COUNTS.` → `THE DAILY RHYTHM · 2 OF 14.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DOES DADI SAY ON THE PORCH BEFORE SUNRISE?`

howItsDone: Fajr is prayed between first light and sunrise, often after the two short sunnah rak'ahs; in the Sunni call for Fajr the caller adds 'as-salatu khayrun min an-nawm'. People set alarms for it, and someone who sleeps through prays it on waking.

fork.setup: a winter camping trip. your phone says Fajr has come in. the tent is warm, it's dark, and everyone's asleep. which way does the dawn line point?
options: sleep; travel makes the morning prayer optional.
get up quietly, pray before the sun rises, then rest if you like.
wait until everyone's up and pray it with breakfast.
fork.reveal: the line is said to exactly this person: warm, sleepy, in bed. prayer is better than sleep, and it's prayed before sunrise. nothing stops you resting after.

adhan.meaning: the call to prayer, given five times a day

Fajr.meaning: dawn; the prayer said at first light

Abu Mahdhura.meaning: a young caller the Prophet taught the adhan to

rak'ahs.meaning: units of prayer: standing, bowing, prostrating, sitting

Abu Dawud.meaning: a classical hadith scholar; his Sunan is a major collection

sources.ref: Sunan Abu Dawud 500 (the Prophet teaches Abu Mahdhura the call, with 'prayer is better than sleep' at Fajr)
Sahih al-Bukhari 657 (Fajr and 'Isha the heaviest prayers for the hypocrites; they would come even crawling)
Sahih Muslim 725 (the two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and what is in it)
Sahih Muslim 684 (whoever sleeps through or forgets a prayer prays it when he remembers)

notes: Shia position on the tathwib (the line is omitted, held to be a later addition): confirm the wording is fair to both Sunni and Shia readers.
Hadith numbers: Abu Dawud 500, Bukhari 657 (also Muslim 651), Muslim 725, Muslim 684 (also Bukhari 597); confirm.
The Arabic of the line 'as-salatu khayrun min an-nawm' is standard; it is a real liturgical line, not a new prayer.
